style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph of a thick, complex shipping logbook and a heavy industrial mechanical date stamp on a plain dark slate desk surface. Top-down 90-degree view, even diffused daylight. The logbook is slightly askew to look handled, with muted paper tones and illegible cropped columns. A heavy, worn brass date stamping mechanism rests on top of the open pages, casting a soft shadow. Minimalist composition, muted neutral palette, editorial elegance, generous negative space.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, wordmarks, signage, UI, UI elements, human hands, people, generic laptop, bare cubes, plain untextured paper, bright colors, toys, clip art
rationale: The article centers heavily on a regulatory timeline, billing, and the importance of stored records and timestamps to settle a dispute. A document flat-lay captures the bureaucratic and evidentiary nature of the 30-day clocks and invoices.
cue: settled by records, not by argument
subject: a shipping ledger and heavy mechanical date stamp
alt_text: Shipping logbook and a heavy mechanical date stamp resting on a dark slate desk.
caption: Under the new shipping rule, stored event timestamps act as the definitive record to settle late-fee disputes.
title: Demurrage Timestamps Document Flatlay
